why: The student works out each variable's role from the code: i is the loop index, so a short name is fine, and c counts the passing scores, so it should be passCount. This links the names to what the code does. The claim that the output stays at 3 is correct (the run printed 3) but has no reason given, so it adds nothing beyond L3.

concepts.quote: i is fine because it is only the loop index. c should be passCount, since it counts the passing scores.
concepts.why: Correctly sees i as a stepper or index, which keeps its short conventional name, and c as a counter that needs a name saying what it counts.

concepts.quote: it is only the loop index
concepts.why: Only names i as the index, without applying the indexing rules to the values.
Makes no claim about how the for statement works.
Makes no claim about the init, test or update.
